extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants and recipients, institutional grants administrators, principal investigators, and institutional officials responsible for NIH award compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements governing consortium agreements, foreign grants, collaborative international research awards, property, auditing, allowable costs, prior approvals, and reporting for NIH-funded awards. Intended to ensure recipients and collaborating organizations meet NIH and federal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and disposition of data produced under the consortium agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A provision addressing ownership and disposition of data produced under the consortium agreement, including whether cell lines, samples or other resources will be freely available to other investigators in the scientific community or will be provided to particular investigators only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium agreements must explicitly state how data and research resources (e.g., cell lines, samples) will be owned, shared, or restricted, so the recipient can meet NIH obligations and expectations for sharing research resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow-down of NIH data sharing and inventions/patent policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A provision making NIH data sharing and inventions and patent policy, including a requirement to report inventions to the recipient, applicable to each consortium participant and its employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure NIH data-sharing, invention reporting, and patent policies are contractually applicable to all consortium participants so the recipient can protect parties’ rights and fulfill NIH reporting and invention disclosure obligations (see Administrative Requirements—Availability of Research Results: Publications, Intellectual Property Rights, and Sharing Research Resources in IIA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for authorship and co-authorship on publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for authorship and co-authorship on publications must be included in the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document authorship/co-authorship criteria and processes in consortium or collaborative agreements to avoid disputes and ensure clarity on publication credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions regarding property, program income, publications, reporting, and audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Include provisions regarding property (other than intellectual property), program income, publications, reporting, and audit necessary for the recipient to fulfill its obligations to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements should cover non-IP property handling, program income treatment, publication rights/processes, required reporting, and audit cooperation to support recipient compliance with award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with UEI and subrecipient reporting under FFATA
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions regarding compliance with requirements for a UEI and subrecipient reporting under FFATA; the recipient must provide the FAIN to all subrecipients to aid in this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow-down provisions and administrative practices must support federal reporting obligations (FFATA), including exchanging unique award/recipient identifiers and necessary award numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of public policy requirements and required assurances/certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of applicable public policy requirements and provisions indicating the intent of each consortium participant to comply, including submission of applicable assurances and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium agreements must state that participants will comply with applicable public policies (e.g., human subjects, animal welfare) and must submit any required assurances/certifications to NIH when applicable (see Public Policy Requirements in IIA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of all required certifications in 2 CFR Part 200.415
rubrics_metrics.description: All required certifications in 2 CFR Part 200.415 must be outlined in the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list and flow down the federal certifications required under 2 CFR 200.415 in subaward/consortium documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate termination if subrecipient suspended, debarred, or excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions regarding immediate termination of the subaward if the direct recipient determines that the subrecipient is suspended, debarred, or otherwise excluded from receiving Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clauses allowing the recipient to terminate/substitute subrecipients promptly upon determining suspension/debarment/exclusion to preserve federal funds and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects assurances and IRB approval for all sites
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient is responsible for ensuring that all sites engaged in human subjects research have an appropriate OHRP-approved assurance and IRB approval of the research consistent with 45 CFR Part 46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must verify assurances and IRB approvals for collaborating sites, obtain additional approvals for adding sites post-award per NIH prior-approval rules, and consult OHRP lists of organizations with approved assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal welfare requirements and IACUC approval; Inter-institutional Assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal welfare requirements that apply to recipients also apply to consortium participants; ensure all sites engaged in research involving live vertebrate animals have an approved Animal Welfare Assurance and valid IACUC approval. If the pass-through entity lacks an Assurance and animal work will be done at a site with an Assurance, the recipient must obtain an Inter-institutional Assurance from OLAW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient must flow animal welfare obligations into agreements, allow institutions discretion about which IACUC reviews protocols, and secure Inter-institutional Assurance when needed so research is conducted under the performance site's animal care program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow-down of government-wide cost principles and NIH cost policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must include in consortium agreements the applicable government-wide cost principles and NIH cost policies described in the Cost Considerations chapter and, as appropriate, requirements related to allowable and unallowable costs in other sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subrecipients must be made subject to the same federal cost principles (e.g., 2 CFR Part 200) and NIH cost policies; examples include applying 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix IX when a university flows funding to a hospital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of federally recognized indirect cost rates or de minimis rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must use an approved federally recognized indirect cost rate negotiated between the subrecipient and the Federal Government. If no such rate exists, use a negotiated rate or the de minimis indirect cost rate of up to 10% MTDC if the subrecipient has never received a negotiated rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure indirect cost rates are documented and applied; SBIR/STTR and certain award classes have special rules. Note F&A reimbursement restrictions for some award classes and that Federal organizations receive limited direct costs and no F&A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient must obtain NIH awarding IC prior approval for certain consortium actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient is responsible for obtaining NIH awarding IC approval for any actions to be undertaken by consortium participants that require prior approval; a recipient may not delegate authorities it does not possess under its NIH award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must secure official written approval (e.g., GMO) before signing subawards when prior approval is required. SBIR/STTR: adding a new subaward post-award requires prior approval and foreign risk assessment via eRA Commons; transfers of work to foreign sites always require awarding IC prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and disposition rules for exempt tangible personal property
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient provides exempt property to a consortium participant or authorizes purchase of property that would be considered exempt if acquired by the recipient, the recipient may vest title in the consortium participant upon transfer or purchase or may reserve the right to do so later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient may set use, disposition, and accountability requirements consistent with NIH's right to transfer title and with Administrative Requirements—Property Management System Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and disposition rules for nonexempt tangible personal property
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient provides nonexempt property to a consortium participant or authorizes purchase of property that would be nonexempt if purchased by the recipient, title must remain with the recipient or be vested in the recipient upon acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient may define use, accountability, and disposition terms provided they are consistent with 2 CFR Part 200.311 and do not impair compliance with federal property requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit compliance for consortium participants per 2 CFR Part 200
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must require consortium participants to comply with the requirements of 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F or 2 CFR Part 200.501, as applicable, for audit of NIH grant funds expended by consortium participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a non-profit consortium participant meets the 2 CFR 200.501 threshold ($1,000,000 aggregate expenditures), recipient must obtain a copy of that audit and take appropriate action to resolve findings that relate to the consortium agreement. Recipient is not responsible for resolving crosscutting findings and may not charge audit costs to NIH unless authorized by 2 CFR 200.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility rules for foreign organizations and international organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign organizations and international organizations are generally eligible to apply for research project grants but are not eligible to submit a modular grant application and are ineligible for certain grant types (e.g., Kirschstein-NRSA institutional training, program project/center/resource/SBIR/STTR, construction grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International organizations are treated as foreign organizations. If a NOFO allows foreign organizations, international organizations may apply; otherwise they may not. Some domestic awards may support projects with a foreign component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a foreign component
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign component is performance of any significant element or segment of the project outside the United States either by the recipient or by a researcher employed by a foreign organization, whether or not grant funds are expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include involvement of human subjects or vertebrate animals at a foreign site, extensive foreign travel for data collection, impact on U.S. foreign policy, collaborations leading to co-authorship, use of foreign facilities/instrumentation, or receipt of foreign financial support. Foreign travel exclusively for consultation is not a foreign component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review additional considerations for foreign applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from foreign organizations or with multiple PD/PIs at foreign organizations will be assessed for whether the project presents special opportunities (unusual talent/resources/populations/conditions) not readily available in the U.S. and whether the project is relevant to the IC mission and has potential to significantly advance health sciences in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These considerations also apply to collaborative international research awards. Research grants from foreign organizations may not be funded unless approved by the IC National Advisory Council or Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of public policy requirements to foreign grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain public policy requirements apply to foreign grants, including Research Misconduct, Animal Welfare, Human Subjects (including 45 CFR Part 46 assurances), Financial Conflict of Interest, Inclusion in Research Design, Lobbying, Debt certification, with some differences for civil rights and debarment/suspension applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil rights requirements do not apply to foreign grants. Foreign governments/public international organizations may be exempt from debarment/suspension certifications. Drug-free workplace requirements may be exempted for foreign applicants where inconsistent with international obligations or foreign laws; check awarding IC guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and payment requirements for foreign grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Application budgets, requests for funds, and financial reports must be stated in U.S. dollars; recipients must maintain grant funds in interest-bearing accounts; drawdowns should be no more than 3 days before funds are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange rate fluctuation costs may be allowable subject to availability of funds and documentation; interest earned in excess of $500/year on advances must be returned in U.S. dollars and reflected on the annual FFR. Payments use PMS operated by PSC; follow PSC/PMS guidance and departmental rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable indirect costs for foreign organizations (fixed 8% MTDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs under grants to foreign and international organizations will be funded at a fixed rate of 8% of modified total direct costs (MTDC), exclusive of tuition/fees, equipment, and domestic subawards over $25,000, with exceptions for American University of Beirut and the World Health Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fixed rate is to support compliance costs (human subjects protection, animal welfare, invention reporting, FCOI, research misconduct, etc.). NIH will not support facilities/capital expenses or depreciation; equipment remains an allowable direct cost. Some normally indirect costs (e.g., rent) may be requested as direct costs and will be evaluated for allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable/unallowable A&R, patient care, and visa costs for foreign grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Major alteration & renovation (A&R) costs are unallowable under foreign grants and domestic grants with foreign components; minor A&R costs are generally allowable. Patient care costs are provided only in exceptional circumstances. Travel visas (including short-term) are generally allowable as part of recruiting costs when an employee/employer relationship exists or when within NOFO scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor A&R may be included in detailed budgets and rebudgeting to accommodate minor A&R requires prior approval of the GMO; visa costs must be justified per the award scope or specific NOFO provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reporting requirements for foreign grants (FFR frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: For SNAP awards to foreign organizations, recipients submit FFR expenditure data at the end of the competitive segment only. For all non-SNAP awards to foreign organizations, recipients are required to submit FFR expenditure data annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are administered in PMS using subaccounts; FFRs must be submitted electronically in U.S. dollars and English, using the currency rate in effect when funds were drawn from PMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in scope rules for foreign grants
rubrics_metrics.description: A change in the performance site within a foreign country or adding a performance site in a different country requires NIH awarding IC prior approval. The transfer of work by a domestic recipient to a foreign component also requires prior approval. NIH no longer recognizes foreign subawards and will not consider requests that would result in a foreign subaward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must seek prior approval before making changes affecting scope or adding foreign sites; follow Administrative Requirements—Changes in Project and Budget—Prior Approval Requirements in IIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of recipient organization for foreign grants
rubrics_metrics.description: A change of recipient organization that involves transfer of a grant to or between foreign organizations or international organizations requires approval of the NIH awarding IC and its National Advisory Council or Board; transfers from foreign to domestic organizations also require awarding IC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients adding or changing a foreign performance site within a funded award must obtain GMO approval before work can be performed at the added/changed site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit requirement threshold for foreign recipients ($750,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign recipients that expend $750,000 (cumulative amount) or more under Federal awards during their fiscal year are required to conduct either a single audit (per 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart F) or a program-specific audit as required by award terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-specific audits are only allowed if all Federal awards expended were from the same Federal agency (or same agency and pass-through entity) and that agency/pass-through entity approves the program-specific audit in advance. International organizations such as WHO, AUB, and UNICEF may be exempt from this audit requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, record retention, and Bayh-Dole obligations for foreign recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: FFR expenditure data must be submitted in U.S. dollars and English; final FFR requires reimbursement for unspent funds; all foreign recipients, contractors, consortium participants, and/or subcontractors must comply with Bayh-Dole invention reporting requirements. Record retention requirements are the same as for domestic recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use currency rate in effect when funds were drawn for FFR; follow HHS Returning Funds instructions for repayments; maintain records per award closeout and NIH record retention requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative International Research Awards structure and disaggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative International Research Awards use a multi-project application structure (PF5/UF5) with separate components for domestic and international subprojects; prior to award international subprojects will be disaggregated and funded as separate RF2 (grants) or UL2 (cooperative agreements) awarded directly to the foreign organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will maintain system links between primary PF5/UF5 awards and disaggregated RF2/UL2 awards for collaborative reporting and programmatic oversight; this structure enables direct legal relationships with foreign collaborators and tracking of international funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and NOFO requirement for Collaborative International Research Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: All research grants/cooperative agreements involving NIH-funded international collaborations must be submitted in response to a NOFO specifically designated for Collaborative International Research Awards; NIH no longer recognizes foreign subawards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not apply to foreign consultants, purchasing unique equipment or supplies from foreign vendors, or non-monetary collaborations (e.g., use of equipment at a foreign site) that would not result in a foreign subaward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated application review and IC National Advisory Council approval for collaborative awards
rubrics_metrics.description: PF5/UF5 applications (with linked RF2/UL2 components) will undergo peer review as a single integrated application but must be reviewed and approved by the IC National Advisory Council or Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Just-in-Time procedures apply to both domestic and foreign applicants; each award (primary and linked) will receive separate Notices of Award and PMS subaccounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction of international collaboration costs with MTDC and indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: For collaborative international research awards, the interaction between the domestic and international partners is not a subrecipient relationship; therefore, costs associated with the international collaboration may not be included in MTDC when calculating indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget preparers should not include such collaboration costs in the domestic applicant’s MTDC for indirect cost calculations; review NIHGPS Chapter 7 and 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart E exceptions in section 16.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, financial separation, and rebudgeting rules for linked collaborative awards
rubrics_metrics.description: All activities must be reported via the RPPR; both primary domestic and international recipients submit RPPRs (information need not be repeated); the domestic recipient provides an attestation in the international recipient’s RPPR. Each linked international award submits separate FFRs; rebudgeting between prime and linked awards is not permitted. Collaborative awards are excluded from automatic carryover unless specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistency between RPPRs; use distinct PMS subaccounts for financial tracking; follow closeout requirements in 8.6 Closeout for all linked awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to records for linked international awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Linked international award recipients are required to provide access to copies of all lab notebooks, all data, and documentation that supports the research outcomes as described in the progress report, to NIH upon request, in accordance with 2 CFR 200.337.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include provisions in agreements and administrative practice to produce lab notebooks/data/documentation to NIH on request; access may be electronic and should align with RPPR reporting frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written agreement minimum elements for collaborative international research projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative research projects must establish written agreements prior to award that include, at minimum: identification of roles/responsibilities of senior/key personnel at each site; procedures for directing and monitoring the research effort; procedures for managing disputes; a provision addressing ownership and disposition of data and research resources; expectations for authorship and co-authorship; and a provision requiring linked international recipients to provide copies of lab notebooks/data/documentation to the domestic recipient at least annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While leveraging elements of consortium agreements is permissible, because the domestic institution is not a pass-through entity, terms implementing pass-through financial/administrative oversight (2 CFR 200.332) are not appropriate in collaborative international award agreements. Ensure written agreements clearly codify roles, monitoring, dispute resolution, data access, and authorship rules.
